translationRepairs: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, a member of the imperial clan, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunli and was registered in the Bordered Blue Banner.
Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, a member of the imperial clan, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunti and was registered in the Bordered Blue Banner.

s0001 names the ancestor 允禵. The character 禵 is tí (Yunti); Yunli would require 禮 (as in 允禮). The proposed Yunti corrects a real romanization error without changing the rest of the accurate idiomatic wording.
Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, an imperial clansman, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunli and belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.
Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, an imperial clansman, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunti and belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.
The same s0001 phrase 允禵 must be Yunti in the literal as in the idiomatic. Yunli misreads 禵; the proposed replacement is the correct reading and otherwise preserves the literal sentence.
For his service he was made Second-rank Defender Prince of the State and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.
For his service he was made Second-rank Defender General of the State and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.
s0036 awards 二等鎮國將軍. 鎮國將軍 is a Qing imperial-clan general rank, not a princely title; replacing "Prince" with "General" restores the correct office while keeping the rest of the sentence.
Under the Tongzhi emperor he was raised to First-rank Defender Prince of the State and made an Inner Minister.
Under the Tongzhi emperor he was raised to First-rank Defender General of the State and made an Inner Minister.
s0058 has 封一等鎮國將軍. As in r0003, 鎮國將軍 is a general rank of the imperial clan, not a prince; "First-rank Defender General of the State" matches the Chinese.
and his grandson Yuzhao held the rank of First-rank Supporter Prince of the State.
and his grandson Yuzhao held the rank of First-rank Supporter General of the State.
s0063 states 孫毓照，一等奉國將軍. 奉國將軍 is likewise an imperial-clan general rank, not a prince; the proposed "Supporter General" corrects that error without rewriting the surrounding kinship phrasing.
Yishan later surrendered the northeastern frontier as well, and the damage he left was even worse.
Yishan later again abandoned the northeastern frontier lands, and the harm he left was even deeper.

s0174 reads 奕山後復棄東北邊地，其貽患尤深. 棄 is abandon (not surrender), 復 is again, and 東北邊地 / 貽患尤深 support "northeastern frontier lands" and deeper/especial harm. The prior "surrendered…as well…even worse" misstates the verbs and softens 復; the proposed wording restores those senses in natural English.
candidateDispositions: Leading Only is English syntax, not part of the name.
